705.title: Cost of Sales and Services
705.tag: Cost of sales and vendor consideration: rebates from suppliers usually reduce cost, not boost revenue.
705.truth: Money a supplier gives back to you is usually a price reduction, not income, because you didn't do anything for the supplier — you just bought more. So vendor rebates and allowances reduce the cost of what you bought unless you provided a distinct service to the vendor at fair value.

analogy.title: The Coffee-Shop Punch Card
analogy.story: When your tenth coffee is free, you didn't 'earn income' from the coffee shop — your coffee just got cheaper on average. Vendor rebates work the same way for a business.

recognition: Consideration from a vendor is a reduction of the purchase price of the vendor's goods/services (705-20-25-1), unless it is payment for a distinct good or service the entity transfers to the vendor (then revenue/other income at up to fair value) or a reimbursement of specific incremental costs.
Recognize rebates contingent on volume when it is probable the milestone will be achieved and the amount is estimable (systematic allocation).

measurement.initial: Allocate rebates to purchases; reduce inventory or expense accordingly.

journalEntries.label: Volume rebate from an appliance supplier
journalEntries.scenario: A portfolio earns a $28,000 year-end volume rebate on appliances purchased for unit renovations (capitalized).
journalEntries.memo: Because the appliances were capitalized, the rebate reduces the asset's cost (and future depreciation), not income.

auditTraps.q: Is a supplier's marketing allowance revenue?
auditTraps.a: Only if it pays for a distinct service provided to the vendor (at fair value); otherwise it reduces cost.

auditTraps.q: Can you recognize a volume rebate before the threshold is hit?
auditTraps.a: Yes if probable and reasonably estimable — recognize systematically as purchases progress toward the milestone.

auditTraps.q: What if the rebate relates to capitalized purchases?
auditTraps.a: It reduces the capitalized cost, not current-period income.

keyParagraphs.subtopic: 20 Accounting for Consideration Received from a Vendor
keyParagraphs.excerpt: Consideration from a vendor includes cash amounts that an entity receives or expects to receive from a vendor (or from other parties that sell the goods or services to the vendor). Consideration from a vendor also includes credit or other items (for example, a coupon or voucher) that the entity can apply against amounts owed to the vendor (or to other parties that sell the goods or services to the vendor). The…

710.title: Compensation—General
710.tag: Compensation: accrue earned wages, bonuses and compensated absences (PTO) as employees work.
710.truth: Employees earn pay by working; the employer's cost exists when the work is done, not when payday arrives. Paid time off that employees have already earned and can carry forward or be paid for is a real obligation, so it is accrued as it's earned.

analogy.title: The Babysitter's Tab
analogy.story: If the babysitter worked Friday and you pay her next Wednesday, you still owed her on Saturday morning. Unused vacation days she's earned are the same — an IOU that builds with every week she works.

recognition: Accrue compensated absences when all conditions are met: the obligation relates to services already rendered, rights vest or accumulate, payment is probable and the amount estimable (710-10-25-1).
Sick pay that accumulates but does not vest may be (but need not be) accrued.
Deferred compensation contracts: accrue the present value of benefits over the service period to full eligibility.

measurement.initial: Current pay rates (or expected rates) applied to earned hours, considering anticipated forfeitures.
measurement.subsequent: True up each period as PTO is used or forfeited.

journalEntries.label: Month-end payroll and PTO accrual for on-site staff
journalEntries.scenario: On-site employees earned $64,000 of wages for the last 9 days of the month (paid next month) and accrued $6,500 of vested PTO.
journalEntries.memo: Include employer payroll taxes on the accrual per policy.

auditTraps.q: Must non-vesting accumulating sick pay be accrued?
auditTraps.a: Not required (710-10-25-7), though permitted.

auditTraps.q: Year-end bonus paid in March — whose expense?
auditTraps.a: The year the service was rendered, if the obligation exists and is estimable (accrue at year-end).

auditTraps.q: PTO policy says 'use it or lose it' at year-end. Accrue at December 31?
auditTraps.a: Generally no carryforward liability beyond unused days that will be paid/used; accrue only the earned amount that vests or accumulates.

710.propertyLens: Payroll allocations for leasing and maintenance staff, bonus accruals and PTO are part of the property's operating expense close.

keyParagraphs.excerpt: An employer shall accrue a liability for employees' compensation for future absences if all of the following conditions are met: (a) The employer's obligation relating to employees' rights to receive compensation for future absences is attributable to employees' services already rendered. (b) The obligation relates to rights that vest or accumulate. Vested rights are those for which the employer has an obligation to…

712.title: Compensation—Nonretirement Postemployment Benefits
712.tag: Nonretirement postemployment benefits (severance, disability, continuation) — accrue when earned or when probable.
712.truth: Benefits paid to former or inactive employees before retirement — severance under an ongoing plan, disability continuation, health-care continuation — are part of the cost of employing people. If they accumulate or vest with service, accrue them as earned; otherwise accrue when payment becomes probable and estimable.

analogy.title: The Company Safety Net
analogy.story: A company promises two weeks of pay per year of service to anyone laid off. Every year an employee works, the promised cushion grows — the company is quietly building a debt to that future layoff.

recognition: Benefits that vest or accumulate with service: accrue under ASC 710 conditions (712-10-25-4).
Other postemployment benefits: accrue under ASC 450 when probable and reasonably estimable (712-10-25-5).
Special termination benefits offered for a short period: recognize when employees accept and the amount is estimable (712-10-25-1).

measurement.initial: Estimate using expected participants, amounts and discounting where appropriate.

journalEntries.label: Accrue severance under an ongoing plan
journalEntries.scenario: A reduction in force makes $210,000 of severance under the company's ongoing plan probable and estimable.

auditTraps.q: 420 vs. 712 for severance?
auditTraps.a: Ongoing benefit arrangements (written or substantive) → 712; one-time benefits → 420.

auditTraps.q: When is a voluntary early-exit incentive recognized?
auditTraps.a: When employees accept the offer and the amount can be estimated (special termination benefits).

auditTraps.q: Are COBRA subsidies postemployment benefits?
auditTraps.a: Yes, continuation of health coverage for former employees is a postemployment benefit under 712.

keyParagraphs.excerpt: Nonretirement postemployment benefits offered as special termination benefits to employees shall be recognized as a liability and a loss when the employees accept the offer and the amount can be reasonably estimated. An employer that offers, for a short period of time, special termination benefits to employees, shall not recognize a loss at the date the offer is made based on the estimated acceptance rate.
Other postemployment benefits that meet the conditions in paragraph 710-10-25-1 shall be accounted for in accordance with Subtopic 710-10.

715.title: Compensation—Retirement Benefits
715.tag: Retirement benefits: defined benefit plans book the funded status; defined contribution plans expense the contribution.
715.truth: A defined-benefit promise is a debt that grows as employees work and is funded by assets that fluctuate. GAAP puts the net funded status (obligation minus plan assets) on the balance sheet and smooths the volatile remeasurements through OCI. A defined-contribution plan is simple: the employer's cost is the contribution it owes for the period.

analogy.title: The Grandparents' Promised College Fund
analogy.story: Grandparents promise to pay whatever a grandchild's college costs in 15 years (defined benefit) and invest money now to cover it. If investments underperform, the shortfall is still theirs. A defined-contribution version is just 'we'll put $200 a month in the fund' — whatever it grows to is the grandchild's risk.

recognition: Single-employer DB plans: recognize the funded status (PBO − fair value of plan assets) as an asset or liability (715-30-25-1).

Net periodic pension cost components: service cost (in operating expense with other compensation), interest cost, expected return on assets, amortization of prior service cost and gains/losses (non-service components presented outside operating income).
Actuarial gains/losses and prior service cost first go to OCI, then amortize (corridor approach or faster).
Defined contribution plans (715-70): expense the contribution for the period; multiemployer plans (715-80): expense required contributions and disclose.

measurement.basis: Actuarial present value (PBO) vs. fair value of plan assets
measurement.initial: Discount benefits using high-quality corporate bond rates; plan assets at fair value.
measurement.subsequent: Remeasure at year-end (and on significant events); amortize AOCI amounts.

journalEntries.label: Record 401(k) employer match for property staff
journalEntries.scenario: The employer match for the month is $18,400, remitted to the plan trustee the next week.
journalEntries.memo: Defined contribution: the cost is the contribution for the period.

auditTraps.q: Where is service cost presented vs. other pension cost components?
auditTraps.a: Service cost with other employee compensation; other components (interest, expected return, amortization) outside operating income (ASU 2017-07).

auditTraps.q: Is the pension liability the ABO or PBO?
auditTraps.a: PBO for pension plans (includes future salary increases); APBO for OPEB.

auditTraps.q: Does a multiemployer plan withdrawal liability get accrued?
auditTraps.a: When withdrawal is probable and the amount estimable (ASC 450).

718.title: Compensation—Stock Compensation
718.tag: Stock comp: measure equity awards at grant-date fair value and expense over the service period.
718.truth: Paying employees with shares or options is still paying them — the company gives up something valuable instead of cash. So the fair value of the award at grant is compensation expense, recognized over the period employees must work to earn it. Whether the award later ends up 'in the money' doesn't change the grant-date cost for equity-classified awards.

analogy.title: Paying the Band in Concert Tickets
analogy.story: A venue pays its band with 100 VIP tickets it could have sold for $200 each. The venue's cost is $20,000 — even though no cash left the building, and even if the tickets later resell for more or less.

recognition: Measure equity-classified awards at grant-date fair value (718-10-30-3); recognize over the requisite service period (graded or straight-line).
Performance conditions: recognize when achievement is probable; market conditions are reflected in grant-date fair value (718-10-30-14) and expense isn't reversed if not met.
Forfeitures: policy election to estimate or account as they occur.
Liability-classified awards (cash-settled, certain puttable) are remeasured each period (718-30).
ASU 2024-01 profits interests: illustrations clarify when profits-interest awards (common in real estate sponsor and REIT LTIP structures) are in scope of 718.

measurement.basis: Grant-date fair value (equity); fair value each period (liability)
measurement.initial: Options: option-pricing model (Black-Scholes, lattice); RSUs: share price at grant (adjusted for dividends not received).
measurement.subsequent: Subsequent: equity awards not remeasured; modifications measured as incremental fair value.

journalEntries.label: Quarterly expense for REIT RSUs
journalEntries.scenario: A REIT grants 40,000 RSUs at $25 fair value, vesting over 4 years (cliff each year, straight-line policy): $1,000,000 total → $62,500 per quarter.
journalEntries.memo: Equity-classified: credit APIC; recognize deferred tax asset where applicable.

auditTraps.q: If options expire underwater, is the expense reversed?
auditTraps.a: No — for service-vested awards, expense reflects grant-date fair value for awards that vest; only forfeitures (failure to vest) reverse expense.

auditTraps.q: Market condition not met — reverse the expense?
auditTraps.a: No. Market conditions are baked into grant-date fair value; expense stays if the service is rendered.

auditTraps.q: Are LTIP units / profits interests stock comp?
auditTraps.a: If they are equity-like interests granted for services, yes — ASU 2024-01's examples help determine whether they're share-based payments (718) or cash bonus/profit-sharing (710).

auditTraps.q: Nonemployee awards?
auditTraps.a: Since ASU 2018-07, nonemployee awards follow 718 too (measured at grant date).

718.propertyLens: REIT and sponsor LTIP units, restricted shares for property executives and profits interests in GP promote vehicles run through 718.

keyParagraphs.excerpt: An entity shall account for the compensation cost from share-based payment transactions in accordance with the fair-value-based method set forth in this Topic. That is, the cost of goods obtained or services received in exchange for awards of share-based compensation generally shall be measured based on the grant-date fair value of the equity instruments issued or on the fair value of the liabilities incurred. The…

Some awards contain a market condition. The effect of a market condition is reflected in the grant-date fair value of an award. (Valuation techniques have been developed to value path-dependent options as well as other options with complex terms. Awards with market conditions, as defined in this Topic, are path-dependent options.) Compensation cost thus is recognized for an award with a market condition provided…

720.title: Other Expenses
720.tag: Other expenses: start-up costs, insurance, property taxes, advertising — mostly expensed as incurred.
720.truth: Many costs create no asset you can point to: opening a new operation, general advertising, charitable gifts. GAAP expenses them as incurred rather than letting companies capitalize hopes. Property taxes are expensed over the period they relate to (the fiscal period of the taxing authority), accrued monthly, because the tax is the price of owning the property during that time.

analogy.title: Opening Night Costs for a New Restaurant
analogy.story: A restaurant's pre-opening staff training, soft-launch party and grand-opening flyers create excitement but no asset you could sell. They are costs of getting started — expensed when incurred, not stored on the balance sheet.

recognition: Start-up and organization costs are expensed as incurred (720-15-25-1) — including lease-up marketing for a new community (but not construction costs capitalizable under 360/970).
Advertising: expense as incurred or the first time the advertising takes place (720-35-25-1).
Real and personal property taxes: accrue monthly over the fiscal period of the taxing authority for which the taxes are levied (720-30).
Insurance costs: premiums amortized over the policy period; retroactive insurance and claims-made policies have specific rules (720-20).
Contributions made: expense (at fair value) when made or unconditionally promised (720-25).

measurement.initial: Measure at amount paid or payable; property taxes at best estimate of the tax for the period.
measurement.subsequent: True-up estimates when bills or assessments arrive.

journalEntries.label: Monthly property-tax accrual
journalEntries.scenario: Estimated annual property tax for a community is $1,080,000, paid in arrears in January.
journalEntries.memo: True up when the assessment/millage is certified; appeals refunds are gain contingencies until realized.

journalEntries.label: Lease-up marketing for a newly delivered building
journalEntries.scenario: Grand-opening advertising and leasing-center events for a new development cost $65,000.
journalEntries.memo: Start-up/advertising costs are expensed — not capitalized into the development.

auditTraps.q: Can property taxes during construction be capitalized?
auditTraps.a: Yes — carrying costs such as property taxes during the development period are capitalized as project costs (ASC 970-340) until the project is substantially complete; after that they're expensed.

auditTraps.q: Is lease-up advertising for a new community capitalized?
auditTraps.a: No — advertising and start-up costs are expensed as incurred (direct-response advertising capitalization was removed).

auditTraps.q: When is a property-tax appeal refund recognized?
auditTraps.a: When realized or when the appeal outcome is final — a gain contingency (450-30).

720.propertyLens: Real estate tax accruals, insurance prepaid amortization, marketing costs and pre-opening costs of new developments are recurring 720 items in the property close.

keyParagraphs.excerpt: Costs of start-up activities, including organization costs, shall be expensed as incurred.

The costs of advertising within the scope of this Subtopic shall be expensed either as incurred or the first time the advertising takes place, except for those costs described in paragraph 720-35-25-1A. The accounting policy selected from these two alternatives shall be applied consistently to similar kinds of advertising activities. Deferring the costs of advertising until the advertising takes place assumes that…

Unlike excise, income, and social security taxes, which are directly related to particular business events, real and personal property taxes are based on the assessed valuation of property (tangible and intangible) as of a given date, as determined by the laws of a state or other taxing authority. The legal liability for such taxes is generally considered as accruing at the moment of occurrence of some specific…

730.title: Research and Development
730.tag: Research and development: expense as incurred — future benefits are too uncertain to capitalize.
730.truth: Research is a bet whose payoff is uncertain and hard to measure, so GAAP refuses to let companies capitalize the bet. R&D costs are expensed as incurred, with narrow exceptions (e.g., assets with alternative future uses; R&D acquired in a business combination is capitalized as IPR&D).

analogy.title: The Chef Testing New Recipes
analogy.story: A chef who spends a month experimenting with new dishes can't claim the failed experiments as 'recipe assets'. The ingredients and time were a cost of trying — the reward only shows up if a dish hits the menu and sells.

recognition: R&D costs are charged to expense when incurred (730-10-25-1).
Equipment, facilities and purchased intangibles with alternative future uses are capitalized and depreciated; the depreciation is R&D expense.
R&D arrangements funded by others (730-20): record a liability if repayment is required regardless of outcome.
IPR&D acquired in an asset acquisition is expensed (if no alternative future use); in a business combination it is capitalized as an indefinite-lived intangible until completion.

measurement.initial: Costs of materials, personnel, contract services, allocated indirect costs.

journalEntries.label: Expense a prop-tech pilot study
journalEntries.scenario: An owner pays a research firm $120,000 to test novel smart-building energy algorithms with uncertain outcomes.
journalEntries.memo: No capitalization — outcome uncertain and no alternative future use.

auditTraps.q: Is IPR&D in an asset acquisition capitalized?
auditTraps.a: No, expensed unless it has an alternative future use; in a business combination it is capitalized (indefinite-lived until complete).

auditTraps.q: Are software development costs R&D?
auditTraps.a: Software for sale follows 985-20 (capitalize after technological feasibility); internal-use software follows 350-40.

auditTraps.q: US GAAP vs IFRS on development costs?
auditTraps.a: IFRS (IAS 38) capitalizes development costs once criteria are met; US GAAP generally expenses R&D.

keyParagraphs.excerpt: Research and development costs encompassed by this Subtopic shall be charged to expense when incurred. As noted in paragraph 730-10-15-4(f), this Topic does not apply to tangible and intangible assets acquired in a business combination, acquired in an acquisition by a not-for-profit entity, or recognized by a joint venture upon formation that are used in research and development activities.

740.title: Income Taxes
740.tag: Income taxes: current tax + deferred tax on temporary differences; uncertain positions need 'more likely than not'.
740.truth: Tax rules and accounting rules disagree about timing. If you've already recorded income that will be taxed later, you owe tax later — a deferred tax liability. If you've recorded expenses you'll deduct later, you'll save tax later — a deferred tax asset, but only if you'll have profits to use it. And tax positions that might not survive an audit can only be booked if they're more likely than not to be sustained.

analogy.title: The Restaurant Tip Jar and the Tax Man
analogy.story: A waiter's credit-card tips land on the paycheck next month, but he earned them tonight. Tonight's 'income' comes with a tax bill that shows up later — a deferred tax liability. If he's promised a deduction he can only use when he has income next year, that future savings is real only if next year's income is likely.

recognition: Current tax = taxes payable/refundable for the year; deferred tax = enacted rate × temporary differences plus carryforwards.
Valuation allowance when it is more likely than not (>50%) that some or all of a DTA will not be realized.
Uncertain tax positions: recognize only if more likely than not to be sustained on technical merits (740-10-25-6); measure as the largest amount >50% likely to be realized on settlement.
ASU 2023-09: enhanced rate-reconciliation categories and income taxes paid disaggregated by jurisdiction (PBEs: annual periods beginning after Dec 15, 2024).
REITs that distribute ≥90% of taxable income and partnerships generally have minimal federal tax; taxable REIT subsidiaries (TRS) and state entity-level taxes still fall under 740.

measurement.basis: Enacted tax rates on temporary differences (undiscounted)
measurement.initial: Deferred taxes measured using enacted rates expected to apply when differences reverse; not discounted.
measurement.subsequent: Remeasure for enacted rate changes in the period of enactment (through continuing operations).

journalEntries.label: Deferred tax on accelerated tax depreciation in a TRS
journalEntries.scenario: A taxable REIT subsidiary's tax depreciation exceeds book depreciation by $400,000 this year; blended enacted rate 25%.
journalEntries.memo: Reverses as book depreciation catches up.

journalEntries.label: Valuation allowance on a TRS net operating loss
journalEntries.scenario: The TRS has a $600,000 DTA from NOLs; negative evidence (cumulative losses) indicates it is not more likely than not to be realized.
journalEntries.memo: Cumulative losses in recent years are significant negative evidence that is hard to overcome.

auditTraps.q: Is a DTA discounted?
auditTraps.a: No — deferred taxes are never discounted.

auditTraps.q: Two-step UTP model?
auditTraps.a: Step 1 recognition: more likely than not to be sustained on technical merits, assuming examination with full knowledge. Step 2 measurement: largest amount >50% likely to be realized.

auditTraps.q: Does a REIT record income tax expense?
auditTraps.a: Generally not at the federal level on distributed income, but state taxes (e.g., Texas margin tax) and TRS income taxes are recorded under 740.

auditTraps.q: When is the effect of a tax rate change recognized?
auditTraps.a: In the period the law is enacted, in income from continuing operations (even if the underlying item was in OCI).

740.propertyLens: Multifamily partnerships and REITs are largely pass-through; the 740 work sits in TRSs (e.g., management or services businesses), state margin taxes and tax-exempt status disclosures.

keyParagraphs.excerpt: An entity shall initially recognize the financial statement effects of a tax position when it is more likely than not, based on the technical merits, that the position will be sustained upon examination. The term more likely than not means a likelihood of more than 50 percent; the terms examined and upon examination also include resolution of the related appeals or litigation processes, if any.
